# ACC/AHA Guideline on Cardiovascular Risk Assessment - 2023

## Section 3: Blood Pressure Management

### 3.1 Blood Pressure Targets

Blood pressure target is recommended to be <130/80 mmHg for most adults with hypertension.

For patients with cardiovascular disease or high risk:
- Target blood pressure should be less than 130/80 mmHg
- Treatment should be initiated at BP >= 130/80 mmHg

### 3.2 Lifestyle Modifications

Lifestyle modifications are recommended for patients with elevated blood pressure:
- Weight reduction
- DASH dietary pattern
- Dietary sodium reduction
- Enhanced intake of dietary potassium
- Physical activity
- Moderation of alcohol intake

### 3.3 Pharmacologic Treatment

Initial antihypertensive therapy:
- Thiazide diuretics
- ACE inhibitors
- Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs)
- Calcium channel blockers

## Section 5: Lipid Management

### 5.1 Statin Therapy

High-intensity statin therapy is recommended for patients with:
- Clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)
- LDL-C >= 190 mg/dL
- Diabetes mellitus with multiple risk factors

### 5.2 LDL-C Goals

For patients with ASCVD:
- LDL-C reduction of >= 50% is recommended
- LDL-C goal <70 mg/dL is reasonable for very high-risk patients

## Section 7: Antiplatelet Therapy

### 7.1 Aspirin

Low-dose aspirin (75-100 mg) is recommended for secondary prevention in patients with established ASCVD.

For primary prevention:
- Aspirin may be considered in select adults aged 40-70 years with higher ASCVD risk
- Aspirin should not be administered routinely for primary prevention in adults >70 years
